```{r}

# Import Colonnade Connections Data

# Installing packages and libraries
```

```{r}
library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)


# Rename column names within connections_data
colnames(connections_data)[6] <- "Major" 
colnames(connections_data)[1] <- "Alum_ID" 
colnames(connections_data)[2] <- "Class" 
colnames(connections_data)[3] <- "Industry" 
colnames(connections_data)[7] <- "Minor" 
colnames(connections_data)[8] <- "Greek_Org"
colnames(connections_data)[10] <- "Activities" 

```

```{r}
#Make a "city", "state" column within connections_data
connections_data <- connections_data %>%
 unite("City_State", City, State, sep = ", ",) %>%
  
#Changing Arlington, VA to Washington, DC
  mutate(City_State = ifelse(City_State == "Arlington, VA", "Washington, DC", City_State))%>%
  mutate(City_State = ifelse(City_State == "Brooklyn, NY", "New York, NY", City_State))%>%
  mutate(City_State = ifelse(City_State == "Washington Dc, DC", "Washington, DC", City_State))%>%
  mutate(City_State = ifelse(City_State == "Washington D.C., DC", "Washington, DC", City_State))
  
```


```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(stringr)

#Delete ", " in Major Column
connections_data$Major_1 <-
  gsub("^, +",
       "", connections_data$Major)

  #New Columns for multiple sports  and major in connections_data
s <- str_split(connections_data$Sports, "; ", simplify = TRUE)
connections_data$Sport_1 <- s[,1]
connections_data$Sport_2 <- s[,2]
connections_data$Sport_3 <- s[,3]
m <- str_split(connections_data$Major, "; |,", simplify = TRUE)
connections_data$Major_1 <- m[,1]
connections_data$Major_2 <- m[,2]





# Factor columns in connections_data
connections_data$Major <- factor(connections_data$Major)
connections_data$City_State <- factor(connections_data$City_State)
connections_data$Class <- factor(connections_data$Class)
connections_data$Industry <- factor(connections_data$Industry)
connections_data$Minor <- factor(connections_data$Minor)
connections_data$Greek_Org <- factor(connections_data$Greek_Org)
connections_data$Sports <- factor(connections_data$Sports)


```

```{r}

#Import rent data
rent_data1 <- read.csv("rent.csv")
 
#Delete unnecessary columns
rent_data2 <- rent_data1 %>% select(-c(Rank, One.year.change, Five.year.change, Rent..2026))

#Delete unnecessary rows within population data
rent_data <- rent_data2[rent_data2$City %in% c(
  "New York, NY",
  "Washington, DC",
  "Atlanta, GA",
  "Charlotte, NC",
  "Dallas, TX",
  "Houston, TX",
  "Richmond, VA",
  "Austin, TX",
  "Charlottesville, VA",
  "Lexington, VA",
  "Nashville, TN",
  "Chicago, IL",
  "Alexandria, VA",
  "Raleigh, NC",
  "Philadelphia, PA",
  "Charleston, SC",
  "San Francisco, CA",
  "Baltimore, MD",
  "Henrico, VA",
  "Boston, MA",
  "Denver, CO",
  "Durham, NC",
  "New Orleans, LA",
  "Roanoke, VA",
  "Birmingham, AL",
  "Pittsburgh, PA",
  "Cincinnati, OH",
  "Fort Worth, TX",
  "Greenville, SC",
  "Tampa, FL"
), ]


#Add any cities left out of data set by hand from zillow 
rent_data <- rent_data %>%
  add_row(City = "Charlottesville, VA", Rent..2025 = "$2,026")%>%
  add_row(City = "Lexington, VA", Rent..2025 = "$1,500")%>%
  add_row(City = "Alexandria, VA", Rent..2025 = "$2,703")%>%

  add_row(City = "Birmingham, AL", Rent..2025 = "$1,150")%>%
  add_row(City = "Greenville, SC", Rent..2025 = "$1,816")
  

rent_data$City <- factor(rent_data$City)

#Rename city column
```

```{r}
#Create City Summary table based on Connections data
#How many alumni in each city

city_summary <- connections_data %>%
  group_by(City_State) %>%
  summarise(
    Alumni_Count = n_distinct(Alum_ID),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Alumni_Count))

```

```{r}
#Create City Sport table based on Connections data
#How many alumni who played each sport in each city
city_sport1 <- connections_data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Sport_1, Sport_2, Sport_3),
    names_to = "Sport_Column",
    values_to = "Sport"

  filter(!is.na(Sport), Sport != "") %>%
  distinct(Alum_ID, City_State, Sport) %>%
```

```{r}
# Import and clean Labor Market Tightness Index dataset


# 2. Import Labor Market Tightness dataset
labor_market_tightness <- read_excel(
  "labor_market_tightness_index.xlsx")
  show_col_types = FALSE

  
# 3. Create reference table matching W&L's top 30 cities to their names in the original dataset
city_lookup <- tribble(
  ~City_State,           ~source_metro,
  "New York, NY",        "New York-Newark-Jersey City, NY-NJ",
  "Washington, DC",      "Washington-Arlington-Alexandria, DC-VA-MD-WV",
  "Atlanta, GA",         "Atlanta-Sandy Springs-Roswell, GA",
  "Charlotte, NC",       "Charlotte-Concord-Gastonia, NC-SC",
  "Dallas, TX",          "Dallas-Fort Worth-Arlington, TX",
  "Houston, TX",         "Houston-Pasadena-The Woodlands, TX",
  "Richmond, VA",        "Richmond, VA",
  "Austin, TX",          "Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos, TX",
  "Charlottesville, VA", "Charlottesville, VA",
  "Lexington, VA",       NA_character_,
  "Nashville, TN",       "Nashville-Davidson--Murfreesboro--Franklin, TN",
  "Chicago, IL",         "Chicago-Naperville-Elgin, IL-IN",
  "Alexandria, VA",      "Washington-Arlington-Alexandria, DC-VA-MD-WV",
  "Raleigh, NC",         "Raleigh-Cary, NC",
  "Philadelphia, PA",    "Philadelphia-Camden-Wilmington, PA-NJ-DE-MD",
  "Charleston, SC",      "Charleston-North Charleston, SC",
  "San Francisco, CA",   "San Francisco-Oakland-Fremont, CA",
  "Baltimore, MD",       "Baltimore-Columbia-Towson, MD",
  "Henrico, VA",         "Richmond, VA",
  "Boston, MA",          "Boston-Cambridge-Newton, MA-NH",
  "Denver, CO",          "Denver-Aurora-Centennial, CO",
  "Durham, NC",          "Durham-Chapel Hill, NC",
  "New Orleans, LA",     "New Orleans-Metairie, LA",
  "Roanoke, VA",         "Roanoke, VA",
  "Birmingham, AL",      "Birmingham, AL",
  "Pittsburgh, PA",      "Pittsburgh, PA",
  "Cincinnati, OH",      "Cincinnati, OH-KY-IN",
  "Fort Worth, TX",      "Dallas-Fort Worth-Arlington, TX",
  "Greenville, SC",      "Greenville-Anderson-Greer, SC",
  "Tampa, FL",           "Tampa-St. Petersburg-Clearwater, FL"
)


# 4. Filter and standardize dataset
labor_tightness_clean <- city_lookup |>
  filter(!is.na(source_metro)) |>      # filter() to exclude cities without a source metro
  inner_join(                            
    labor_market_tightness,
    by = join_by(source_metro == City_State)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    # Identify destinations using a shared metro value
    metro_proxy = City_State %in% c(
      "Alexandria, VA",
      "Henrico, VA",
      "Fort Worth, TX"
    )
  ) |>
  select(
    City_State,
    Tightness_Index,
    cbsa_code,
    Rank,
    source_metro,
    metro_proxy
  )

```

```{r}
city_master1 <- city_summary %>%
  left_join(population_data, by = "City_State") %>%
  left_join(rent_data, by = "City_State") %>%
  left_join(labor_tightness_clean, by = "City_State")
  

city_master <- city_master1[city_master1$City_State %in% c(
  "New York, NY",
  "Washington, DC",
  "Atlanta, GA",
  "Charlotte, NC",
  "Dallas, TX",
  "Houston, TX",
  "Richmond, VA",

  "Fort Worth, TX",
  "Greenville, SC",
  "Tampa, FL"
), ]

#Widen Connections Data
city_sport_wide <- city_sport %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Sport,
    values_from = Alumni_Count,
    values_fill = 0,
  )
city_industry_wide <- city_industry %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Industry,
    values_from = Alumni_Count,
    values_fill = 0,
    names_prefix = "Industry_"
  )
city_greekOrg_wide <- city_greekOrg %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Greek_Org,
    values_from = Alumni_Count,
    values_fill = 0,
  )
city_major_wide <- city_major %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Alumni_Major,
    values_from = Alumni_Count,
    values_fill = 0,
    names_prefix = "Major_"
  )

city_master <- city_master %>%
  left_join(city_sport_wide, by = "City_State") %>%
  left_join(city_industry_wide, by = "City_State") %>%
  left_join(city_greekOrg_wide, by = "City_State") %>%
  left_join(city_major_wide, by = "City_State") %>%
  mutate(
    across(where(is.numeric), ~ replace_na(.x, 0))
  )

city_master <- city_master %>%
  rename(Rent_2025 = Rent..2025) %>% 
  mutate(Rent_2025 = as.numeric(str_replace_all(Rent_2025, "[$,]", "")))


```


```{r}
# Merging industry columns into broader categories and renaming them


# then the columns are added together. Backticks are needed around any column
# name that contains spaces, hyphens, slashes, or ampersands.
city_master <- city_master %>%
  mutate(

    # Finance (Finance + PE + all other finance subcategories)
    Industry_Finance =
      coalesce(Industry_Finance, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Finance - Private Equity`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Finance - Investment Banking`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Finance - Investment Management`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Finance - Hedge Fund`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Finance - Venture Capital`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Finance - Commercial Banking`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Finance - Consumer Banking`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Finance - Sales & Trading`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Finance - LBO`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Investments/Finance`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Banking/Commerce`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Financial Services`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Financial Services - Diversified`, 0),

    # Insurance
    Industry_Insurance =
      coalesce(Industry_Insurance, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Insurance/Diversified Financials`, 0),

    # Consulting
    Industry_Consulting =
      coalesce(Industry_Consulting, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Professional Services`, 0),

    # Human Resources
    Industry_Human_Resources =
      coalesce(`Industry_Human Resources`, 0),

    # Accounting (single column; coalesce just fills NAs with 0)
    Industry_Accounting =
      coalesce(Industry_Accounting, 0),

    # Law
    Industry_Legal =
      coalesce(`Industry_Legal Services`, 0),

    # Technology
    Industry_Technology =
      coalesce(`Industry_Tech - Software`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Tech - Services`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Tech - Internet Services`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Tech - Hardware`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Tech - Consumer Electronics`, 0) +
      coalesce(Industry_Computer, 0) +
      coalesce(Industry_Electronics, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Data Analytics`, 0) +
      coalesce(Industry_Telecommunications, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Healthcare - Biotechnology`, 0),

    # Healthcare & Life Sciences
    Industry_Healthcare =
      coalesce(`Industry_Healthcare - Delivery/Provider`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Healthcare - Services/Other`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Healthcare - Medical Devices`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Healthcare - Pharmaceuticals`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Healthcare - Medicine/Research`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Scientific Research`, 0),

    # Government, Policy & Defense
    Industry_Government =
      coalesce(`Industry_Government - Federal`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Government - State/Local`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Government - Other`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Government - Armed Forces`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Government - International`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Political Campaign`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_International Development`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Aerospace & Defense`, 0),

    # Education
    Industry_Education =
      coalesce(`Industry_Education - Higher Ed`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Education - Pre K - 12`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Education - Other`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Education/Schools`, 0),

    # Nonprofit & Social Impact
    Industry_Nonprofit =
      coalesce(`Industry_Non-Profit Organization`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Public Charity`, 0) +
      coalesce(Industry_Foundation, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Foundation - Other`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Organizations/Associations/Society`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Development-Fundraising`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Human/Social Services`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Economic/Community Development`, 0) +
      coalesce(Industry_Religion, 0),

    # Real Estate
    Industry_Real_Estate =
      coalesce(`Industry_Real Estate - Commercial`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Real Estate - Finance`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Real Estate - Residential`, 0) +
      coalesce(Industry_Construction, 0) +
      coalesce(Industry_Architecture, 0),

    # Engineering
    Industry_Engineering =
      coalesce(Industry_Engineering, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Engineering & Science`, 0),

    # Energy & Industrial
    Industry_Energy_Industrial =
      coalesce(Industry_Energy, 0) +
      coalesce(Industry_Utilities, 0) +
      coalesce(Industry_Environment, 0) +
      coalesce(Industry_Manufacturing, 0) +
      coalesce(Industry_Chemical, 0) +
      coalesce(Industry_Agriculture, 0) +
      coalesce(Industry_Transportation, 0),

    # Media, Marketing & Creative
    Industry_Media_Marketing =
      coalesce(`Industry_Advertising/Public Relations`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Print/Publishing`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Broadcast/Film/Multimedia`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Arts/Culture`, 0),

    # Consumer, Retail & Hospitality
    Industry_Consumer_Retail =
      coalesce(`Industry_Consumer Products`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Retail/Wholesale`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Food/Beverage`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Food Products`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Textiles & Apparel`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Hospitality Services`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Entertainment/Leisure/Sports`, 0),

    # Other / Undecided (Industry_ is the blank-named column)
    Industry_Other =
      coalesce(`Industry_`, 0) +
      coalesce(`Industry_Bus. Other`, 0) +
      coalesce(Industry_Service, 0)
  )
```

```{r}
# Importing and cleaning US cities latitudes and longitudes database 
# Used USPS PostalPro GIS data to add one missing observation (ID #29882) measuring the latitude and longitude for Henrico, VA.

cities_df <- read.csv("cleaned_us_cities.csv")

#Make a "city", "state" column
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

cities_df <- cities_df %>% 
  unite(col = "City_State", CITY, STATE_CODE, sep = ", ")

# Keep cities of interest 
target_cities <- c(
  "New York, NY",
  "Washington, DC",
  "Atlanta, GA",
  "Charlotte, NC",
  "Dallas, TX",
  "Houston, TX",
  "Richmond, VA",
  "Austin, TX",
  "Charlottesville, VA",
  "Lexington, VA",
  "Nashville, TN",
  "Chicago, IL",
  "Alexandria, VA",
  "Raleigh, NC",
  "Philadelphia, PA",
  "Charleston, SC",
  "San Francisco, CA",
  "Baltimore, MD",
  "Henrico, VA",
  "Boston, MA",
  "Denver, CO",
  "Durham, NC",
  "New Orleans, LA",
  "Roanoke, VA",
  "Birmingham, AL",
  "Pittsburgh, PA",
  "Cincinnati, OH",
  "Fort Worth, TX",
  "Greenville, SC",
  "Tampa, FL"
)

# 2. Filter the dataset to keep only rows matching city list 
city_coordinates_df <- cities_df %>%
  filter(City_State %in% target_cities) %>%
  distinct(City_State, .keep_all = TRUE)

# 3. Join city_coordinates to city_master

city_master <- city_master %>%
  left_join(city_coordinates_df, by = "City_State")
  
```
